S.FORM: tee=ku pu-a-iisua ni-ki-anal-a kaisisi mikauŋu.
S.PHON: teeku puaiisua nikianaɾa kaiʂiʂi mikauŋu
S.FORM: teeku puaiisua nikianara kaisisi mikaungu.
S.PHON: teeku puaiisua nikiana[r|ɾ]a kaiʂiʂi mikauŋu
S.TRANSL: I shall talk about the origin of the ritual ceremony.

S.FORM: sua ni-ki-anal-a mikauŋu ia, Ɂuuna u-rucini.
S.PHON: sua nikianaɾa mikauŋu ia ʔuuna urutʂini
S.FORM: sua nikianara mikaungu ia, 'uuna urucini.
S.PHON: sua nikiana[r|ɾ]a mikauŋu ia ʔuuna u[r|ɾ]utʂini
S.TRANSL: There are two sources for the origin of the ritual ceremony mikauŋu.

S.FORM: ni-ki-anal-a mati-cani pu-a-iisua tapucalakai.
S.PHON: nikianaɾa matiʦani puaiisua tapuʦaɾakai
S.FORM: nikianara maticani puaiisua tapucarakai.
S.PHON: nikiana[r|ɾ]a matiʦani puaiisua tapuʦa[r|ɾ]akai
S.TRANSL: The first origin talks about little people.

S.FORM: miana, miana, Ɂuuna ta-cini nanmaluanə ni-m-avici talimau mu-a-kusa nəmər-a.
S.PHON: miana miana ʔuuna tatʂini nanmaɾuanə nimavitʂi taɾimau muakusa nəməra
S.FORM: miana, miana, 'uuna tacini nanmaruane nimavici tarimau muakusa nemera.
S.PHON: miana miana ʔuuna tatʂini nanma[r|ɾ]uane nimavitʂi ta[r|ɾ]imau muakusa neme[r|ɾ]a
S.TRANSL: Long, long ago, a young man went to the mountain with a hoe.

S.FORM: tee=kirimi tee=kaən-a cau tanasən panansi miaa-sua ia, ni-mu-səɁəc-ai ka-vaŋvaŋ cau mamanai.
S.PHON: teekirimi teekaəna ʦau tanasən pananʂi miaasua ia nimusəʔəʦai kavaŋvaŋ ʦau mamanai
S.FORM: teekirimi teekaena cau tanasen panansi miaasua ia, nimuse'ecai kavangvang cau mamanai.
S.PHON: teeki[r|ɾ]imi teekaena ʦau tanasen pananʂi miaasua ia nimuseʔeʦai kavaŋvaŋ ʦau mamanai
S.TRANSL: He was to look for food for people in the village because all people in the world were starving.

S.FORM: makasua=cu nanmaluanə tia=mu-raanə cau=kia.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu nanmaɾuanə tiamuraanə ʦaukia
S.FORM: makasuacu nanmaruane tiamuraane caukia.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu nanma[r|ɾ]uane tiamu[r|ɾ]aane ʦaukia
S.TRANSL: In that way, the young man would help his own people.

S.FORM: tee=kirimi kaən-a cau ni-mu-lavu.
S.PHON: teekirimi kaəna ʦau nimuɾavu
S.FORM: teekirimi kaena cau nimuravu.
S.PHON: teeki[r|ɾ]imi kaena ʦau nimu[r|ɾ]avu
S.TRANSL: He was to search for food for the hungry people.

S.FORM: ʔu-rupaca talimau k<um>a-kauru ramisi naminsi.
S.PHON: ʔurupaʦa taɾimau kumakauru ramiʂi naminʂi
S.FORM: 'urupaca tarimau k<um>akauru ramisi naminsi.
S.PHON: ʔu[r|ɾ]upaʦa ta[r|ɾ]imau kumakau[r|ɾ]u [r|ɾ]amiʂi naminʂi
S.TRANSL: He used the hoe to dig the roots of ivy, similar to a sweet potato.

S.FORM: makasua=cu nanmaluanə kipatəcə k<um>a-kauru kə-sikarə ʔənai.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu nanmaɾuanə kipatəʦə kumakauru kəʂikarə ʔənai
S.FORM: makasuacu nanmaruane kipatece k<um>akauru kesikare 'enai.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu nanma[r|ɾ]uane kipateʦe kumakau[r|ɾ]u keʂika[r|ɾ]e ʔenai
S.TRANSL: In that way the young man dug deep into the ground with great effort.

S.FORM: ʔacu ni-ki-a-lakau=kiai taruku.
S.PHON: ʔaʦu nikiaɾakaukiai taruku
S.FORM: 'acu nikiarakaukiai taruku.
S.PHON: ʔaʦu nikia[r|ɾ]akaukiai ta[r|ɾ]uku
S.TRANSL: A cave appeared.

S.FORM: tara-kusa ʔəna-ʔənai, misaini ʔuuna ʔəna-ʔənai taruku cau ma-ʔuʔura mata ʔuuna ni-pa-ari-a nua-nuamani pi-piniŋi.
S.PHON: tarakusa ʔənaʔənai misaini ʔuuna ʔənaʔənai taruku ʦau maʔuʔura mata ʔuuna nipaaria nuanuamani pipiniŋi
S.FORM: tarakusa 'ena'enai, misaini 'uuna 'ena'enai taruku cau ma'u'ura mata 'uuna nipaaria nuanuamani pipiningi.
S.PHON: ta[r|ɾ]akusa ʔenaʔenai misaini ʔuuna ʔenaʔenai ta[r|ɾ]uku ʦau maʔuʔu[r|ɾ]a mata ʔuuna nipaa[r|ɾ]ia nuanuamani pipiniŋi
S.TRANSL: He looked down below the ground, and wondered why there were little people in the cave and the things inside were exposed to the sun outside.

S.FORM: makasua=cu nanmaluanə pa-cəpə-cəpəŋ, "tee=kita ma-ka-naanu mata-ʔənai tee=kiri-kirimi cipunu tia=si-a-rupaca mata-ʔənai."
S.PHON: makasuaʦu nanmaɾuanə paʦəpəʦəpəŋ teekita makanaanu mataʔənai teekirikirimi tʂipunu tiaʂiarupaʦa mataʔənai
S.FORM: makasuacu nanmaruane pacepecepeng, "teekita makanaanu mata'enai teekirikirimi cipunu tiasiarupaca mata'enai."
S.PHON: makasuaʦu nanma[r|ɾ]uane paʦepeʦepeŋ teekita makanaanu mataʔenai teeki[r|ɾ]iki[r|ɾ]imi tʂipunu tiaʂia[r|ɾ]upaʦa mataʔenai
S.TRANSL: The young man thought, I shall look for a vine and use it to go down.

S.FORM: ʔ<um>a-laucu m-ətəa cipunu ma-cuŋu-cuŋucu k<um>ini na ŋacaʔə kaalu maica=cu ʔinia mata-ʔənai.
S.PHON: ʔumaɾauʦu mətəa tʂipunu maʦuŋuʦuŋuʦu kumini na ŋaʦaʔə kaaɾu maiʦaʦu ʔinia mataʔənai
S.FORM: '<um>araucu metea cipunu macungucungucu k<um>ini na ngaca'e kaaru maicacu 'inia mata'enai.
S.PHON: ʔuma[r|ɾ]auʦu metea tʂipunu maʦuŋuʦuŋuʦu kumini na ŋaʦaʔe kaa[r|ɾ]u maiʦaʦu ʔinia mataʔenai
S.TRANSL: Finally, he found a vine and kept extending it to make it long enough. He could then tie it to the tree stump and go down below the ground using the vine.

S.FORM: ara-kicacə cau ma-ʔuʔura, "niani sua ni-i-vatu cau makai tipari?"
S.PHON: arakiʦaʦə ʦau maʔuʔura niani sua niivatu ʦau makai tipari
S.FORM: arakicace cau ma'u'ura, "niani sua niivatu cau makai tipari?"
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]akiʦaʦe ʦau maʔuʔu[r|ɾ]a niani sua niivatu ʦau makai tipa[r|ɾ]i
S.TRANSL: The little people were surprised (and said), "Who has come? He looks like a giant?"

S.FORM: mata-cuvu-cuvuŋ ka-vaŋvaŋ cau ma-ʔuʔura.
S.PHON: mataʦuvuʦuvuŋ kavaŋvaŋ ʦau maʔuʔura
S.FORM: matacuvucuvung kavangvang cau ma'u'ura.
S.PHON: mataʦuvuʦuvuŋ kavaŋvaŋ ʦau maʔuʔu[r|ɾ]a
S.TRANSL: All the little people gathered together.

S.FORM: maa-kari na nanmaluanə, "niani sua=kasu?"
S.PHON: maakari na nanmaɾuanə niani suakasu
S.FORM: maakari na nanmaruane, "niani suakasu?"
S.PHON: maaka[r|ɾ]i na nanma[r|ɾ]uane niani suakasu
S.TRANSL: They said to the young man, "Who are you?"

S.FORM: tuturu-nu nanmaluanə, "sua iiku ia, cau mamanai."
S.PHON: tuturunu nanmaɾuanə sua iiku ia ʦau mamanai
S.FORM: tuturunu nanmaruane, "sua iiku ia, cau mamanai."
S.PHON: tutu[r|ɾ]unu nanma[r|ɾ]uane sua iiku ia ʦau mamanai
S.TRANSL: The young man told him, "I'm a person in the world."

S.FORM: ki-a-vali sua nanmaluanə na cau ma-ʔuʔura, "tee=ku ʔani-misa-ini kamua?"
S.PHON: kiavaɾi sua nanmaɾuanə na ʦau maʔuʔura teeku ʔanimisaini kamua
S.FORM: kiavari sua nanmaruane na cau ma'u'ura, "teeku 'animisaini kamua?"
S.PHON: kiava[r|ɾ]i sua nanma[r|ɾ]uane na ʦau maʔuʔu[r|ɾ]a teeku ʔanimisaini kamua
S.TRANSL: The young man replied, "What shall I call you?"

S.FORM: m-ali-vali cau ma-ʔuʔura, "sua iikimi ia, tapucalakai."
S.PHON: maɾivaɾi ʦau maʔuʔura sua iikimi ia tapuʦaɾakai
S.FORM: marivari cau ma'u'ura, "sua iikimi ia, tapucarakai."
S.PHON: ma[r|ɾ]iva[r|ɾ]i ʦau maʔuʔu[r|ɾ]a sua iikimi ia tapuʦa[r|ɾ]akai
S.TRANSL: The little people replied, "We are the little people."

S.FORM: aranai=cu mia-sua pa-tara-kanaŋə.
S.PHON: aranaiʦu miasua patarakanaŋə
S.FORM: aranaicu miasua patarakanange.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]anaiʦu miasua pata[r|ɾ]akanaŋe
S.TRANSL: Since then they knew each other.

S.FORM: ki-a-suanai nanmaluanə, na tapucalakai, "niani sua suanai ni-pa-ari-a=mu ta-piniŋ-a. iisi?"
S.PHON: kiasuanai nanmaɾuanə na tapuʦaɾakai niani sua suanai nipaariamu tapiniŋa iiʂi
S.FORM: kiasuanai nanmaruane, na tapucarakai, "niani sua suanai nipaariamu tapininga. iisi?"
S.PHON: kiasuanai nanma[r|ɾ]uane na tapuʦa[r|ɾ]akai niani sua suanai nipaa[r|ɾ]iamu tapiniŋa iiʂi
S.TRANSL: The young man asked the little people, "What (which crops) did you expose to the sun outside there?"

S.FORM: m-ali-vali tapucalakai, "vinaʔə, viaru, nəpənəpə, ʔaricaŋ."
S.PHON: maɾivaɾi tapuʦaɾakai vinaʔə viaru nəpənəpə ʔariʦaŋ
S.FORM: marivari tapucarakai, "vina'e, viaru, nepenepe, 'aricang."
S.PHON: ma[r|ɾ]iva[r|ɾ]i tapuʦa[r|ɾ]akai vinaʔe via[r|ɾ]u nepenepe ʔa[r|ɾ]iʦaŋ
S.TRANSL: The little people replied, "Millet, corn, long beans and beans."

S.FORM: makinai nanmaluanə na tapucalakai, "tavalaʔə=kara=kamu mu-a-vua ʔikua raapə vinaʔə mata əvəka mu-a-vua ʔikua?"
S.PHON: makinai nanmaɾuanə na tapuʦaɾakai tavaɾaʔəkarakamu muavua ʔikua raapə vinaʔə mata əvəka muavua ʔikua
S.FORM: makinai nanmaruane na tapucarakai, "tavara'ekarakamu muavua 'ikua raape vina'e mata eveka muavua 'ikua?"
S.PHON: makinai nanma[r|ɾ]uane na tapuʦa[r|ɾ]akai tava[r|ɾ]aʔeka[r|ɾ]akamu muavua ʔikua [r|ɾ]aape vinaʔe mata eveka muavua ʔikua
S.TRANSL: The young man asked the little people for (something), "Can you give me some millet and bean seeds?"

S.FORM: kaʔanə m-ali-vali tapucalakai, ʔaisi=pa pa-cəpə-cəpəŋ tia=pa ikar-ən manasii vua-ənə=cu raapə mata əvəka
S.PHON: kaʔanə maɾivaɾi tapuʦaɾakai ʔaiʂipa paʦəpəʦəpəŋ tiapa ikarən manaʂii vuaənəʦu raapə mata əvəka
S.FORM: ka'ane marivari tapucarakai, 'aisipa pacepecepeng tiapa ikaren manasii vuaenecu raape mata eveka
S.PHON: kaʔane ma[r|ɾ]iva[r|ɾ]i tapuʦa[r|ɾ]akai ʔaiʂipa paʦepeʦepeŋ tiapa ika[r|ɾ]en manaʂii vuaeneʦu [r|ɾ]aape mata eveka
S.TRANSL: The little people did not reply, as they were considering having him work for them before giving him millet and bean seeds.

S.FORM: m-ali-vali tapucalakai, "tavalaʔ-ən mu-a-vua kasua, nakai tee=pa=kasu ikar-ən=mia. mu-a-ʔuna=pa miasi mu-a-raanə kimia."
S.PHON: maɾivaɾi tapuʦaɾakai tavaɾaʔən muavua kasua nakai teepakasu ikarənmia muaʔunapa miaʂi muaraanə kimia
S.FORM: marivari tapucarakai, "tavara'en muavua kasua, nakai teepakasu ikarenmia. mua'unapa miasi muaraane kimia."
S.PHON: ma[r|ɾ]iva[r|ɾ]i tapuʦa[r|ɾ]akai tava[r|ɾ]aʔen muavua kasua nakai teepakasu ika[r|ɾ]enmia muaʔunapa miaʂi mua[r|ɾ]aane kimia
S.TRANSL: The little people replied, "We can give them to you, but you will have to work for us, and live here to help us."

S.FORM: pa-cəpə-cəpəŋ sua nanmaluanə, "tee=kita um-ala raapə mata əvəka."
S.PHON: paʦəpəʦəpəŋ sua nanmaɾuanə teekita umaɾa raapə mata əvəka
S.FORM: pacepecepeng sua nanmaruane, "teekita umara raape mata eveka."
S.PHON: paʦepeʦepeŋ sua nanma[r|ɾ]uane teekita uma[r|ɾ]a [r|ɾ]aape mata eveka
S.TRANSL: The young man was considering, "We would like to get millet and bean seeds."

S.FORM: m-ali-vali nanmaluanə na tapucalakai, "əəʔə," misa.
S.PHON: maɾivaɾi nanmaɾuanə na tapuʦaɾakai əəʔə misa
S.FORM: marivari nanmaruane na tapucarakai, "ee'e," misa.
S.PHON: ma[r|ɾ]iva[r|ɾ]i nanma[r|ɾ]uane na tapuʦa[r|ɾ]akai eeʔe misa
S.TRANSL: The young man replied to the little people saying, "Yes."

S.FORM: makasua=cu nanmaluanə mu-a-ʔuna ʔinia mu-a-raanə putu-kia-kiau mata-lava=cu ru-vana.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu nanmaɾuanə muaʔuna ʔinia muaraanə putukiakiau mataɾavaʦu ruvana
S.FORM: makasuacu nanmaruane mua'una 'inia muaraane putukiakiau mataravacu ruvana.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu nanma[r|ɾ]uane muaʔuna ʔinia mua[r|ɾ]aane putukiakiau mata[r|ɾ]avaʦu [r|ɾ]uvana
S.TRANSL: In that way the young man lived there and helped them with their work until the evening.

S.FORM: tee=cu k<um>a-kaənə uuru, cəʔəra-i nanmaluanə ni-pu-ʔucipi tapucalakai uuru ma-kaŋəcə maamia.
S.PHON: teeʦu kumakaənə uuru ʦəʔərai nanmaɾuanə nipuʔutʂipi tapuʦaɾakai uuru makaŋəʦə maamia
S.FORM: teecu k<um>akaene uuru, ce'erai nanmaruane nipu'ucipi tapucarakai uuru makangece maamia.
S.PHON: teeʦu kumakaene uu[r|ɾ]u ʦeʔe[r|ɾ]ai nanma[r|ɾ]uane nipuʔutʂipi tapuʦa[r|ɾ]akai uu[r|ɾ]u makaŋeʦe maamia
S.TRANSL: When they were to eat rice, the young man saw that the little people had cooked only a little rice.

S.FORM: "tee=kita ma-ka-naanu k<um>a-kaənə? ma-naasə kaʔanə=kita tia=ku-vəcərəkə si ma-kaŋəcə uuru."
S.PHON: teekita makanaanu kumakaənə manaasə kaʔanəkita tiakuvəʦərəkə ʂi makaŋəʦə uuru
S.FORM: "teekita makanaanu k<um>akaene? manaase ka'anekita tiakuvecereke si makangece uuru."
S.PHON: teekita makanaanu kumakaene manaase kaʔanekita tiakuveʦe[r|ɾ]eke ʂi makaŋeʦe uu[r|ɾ]u
S.TRANSL: "How shall we eat? It is possible that we won't eat until we are full because there is little rice."

S.FORM: ma-kasi tapucalakai, ʔinia, "misaini=kasu kaʔanə k<um>a-kaənə uuru?"
S.PHON: makaʂi tapuʦaɾakai ʔinia misainikasu kaʔanə kumakaənə uuru
S.FORM: makasi tapucarakai, 'inia, "misainikasu ka'ane k<um>akaene uuru?"
S.PHON: makaʂi tapuʦa[r|ɾ]akai ʔinia misainikasu kaʔane kumakaene uu[r|ɾ]u
S.TRANSL: The little people asked him, "Why don't you eat rice?"

S.FORM: m-ali-vali nanmaluanə, "ku-ʔulu-a=kamu k<um>a-kaənə ni-ku-tiŋasə=mu kaən-a ia, tia=kaən-a=maku."
S.PHON: maɾivaɾi nanmaɾuanə kuʔuɾuakamu kumakaənə nikutiŋasəmu kaəna ia tiakaənamaku
S.FORM: marivari nanmaruane, "ku'uruakamu k<um>akaene nikutingasemu kaena ia, tiakaenamaku."
S.PHON: ma[r|ɾ]iva[r|ɾ]i nanma[r|ɾ]uane kuʔu[r|ɾ]uakamu kumakaene nikutiŋasemu kaena ia tiakaenamaku
S.TRANSL: The young man replied, "You eat first. I'll eat what is left by you."

S.FORM: mati-rupaŋə tapucalakai k<um>a-kaənə, caanpai maamia nanmaluanə, tia=mata-kauru uuru, kuu=cu ku-vəcərəkə si ma-kaŋəcə=cu ni-ku-tiŋasə tapucalakai.
S.PHON: matirupaŋə tapuʦaɾakai kumakaənə ʦaanpai maamia nanmaɾuanə tiamatakauru uuru kuuʦu kuvəʦərəkə ʂi makaŋəʦəʦu nikutiŋasə tapuʦaɾakai
S.FORM: matirupange tapucarakai k<um>akaene, caanpai maamia nanmaruane, tiamatakauru uuru, kuucu kuvecereke si makangececu nikutingase tapucarakai.
S.PHON: mati[r|ɾ]upaŋe tapuʦa[r|ɾ]akai kumakaene ʦaanpai maamia nanma[r|ɾ]uane tiamatakau[r|ɾ]u uu[r|ɾ]u kuuʦu kuveʦe[r|ɾ]eke ʂi makaŋeʦeʦu nikutiŋase tapuʦa[r|ɾ]akai
S.TRANSL: When the little people finished eating, he was about to fill (a bowl) with rice, he did not eat until he is full because very little rice was left by the little people.

S.FORM: paira makasua tan-taniarə.
S.PHON: paira makasua tantaniarə
S.FORM: paira makasua tantaniare.
S.PHON: pai[r|ɾ]a makasua tantania[r|ɾ]e
S.TRANSL: It was usually in that way everyday.

S.FORM: pa-cəpə-cəpəŋ tapucalakai tee=cu=mita pa-li-aluma-n nanmaluanə si i-tumulu ava kaən-ən.
S.PHON: paʦəpəʦəpəŋ tapuʦaɾakai teeʦumita paɾiaɾuman nanmaɾuanə ʂi itumuɾu ava kaənən
S.FORM: pacepecepeng tapucarakai teecumita pariaruman nanmaruane si itumuru ava kaenen.
S.PHON: paʦepeʦepeŋ tapuʦa[r|ɾ]akai teeʦumita pa[r|ɾ]ia[r|ɾ]uman nanma[r|ɾ]uane ʂi itumu[r|ɾ]u ava kaenen
S.TRANSL: The little people were considering chasing him away because he ate a lot.

S.FORM: "kaʔanə taavalaʔ-ən um-əkəərə si tia=ku-vaŋəvaŋ-ən=kiai kaən-a=mita."
S.PHON: kaʔanə taavaɾaʔən uməkəərə ʂi tiakuvaŋəvaŋənkiai kaənamita
S.FORM: "ka'ane taavara'en umekeere si tiakuvangevangenkiai kaenamita."
S.PHON: kaʔane taava[r|ɾ]aʔen umekee[r|ɾ]e ʂi tiakuvaŋevaŋenkiai kaenamita
S.TRANSL: "We could not keep him because he might eat up all our food."

S.FORM: makasua=cu tapucalakai mati-ʔaraŋə mu-a-pucu raapə vinaʔə mata tuutu taparu mu-a-vua ʔinia, "mu-caan-a=cu kəəcə=kasu!"

S.FORM: mia ʔaisi=pa ca-caanə taka-ci-cini pu-a-kari-kari, "nəpənəpə," misa, ma-ʔicəpə nuu ru-aimi ŋanai nəpənəpə.

S.PHON: nipapavitʂi tapuʦaɾakai na nanmaɾuanə kari nuu itumuɾutʂi niaɾamu kaəna ia ʔakuni ruaimi puakari kimia
S.FORM: nipapavici tapucarakai na nanmaruane kari, "nuu itumuruci niaramu kaena ia, 'akuni ruaimi puakari, kimia."

S.TRANSL: As for the girl 'Usu, she was surrounded by the big fire, which was approching her on top (of a tree).

S.TRANSL: The men all heard the voice sounding like 'Usu shouting "Father, Mother, Father, Mother, rescue me!"

S.TRANSL: They looked at it carefully and wondered why something looking like 'Usu's face was going up with the fire smoke.

S.PHON: makasuaʦu musu[r|ɾ]upaŋe nama[r|ɾ]e ʦapuku

S.PHON: makasuaʦu puaiʔi tanasa

S.PHON: makaaʦaŋe kiasuanai ʦau tanasa tʂinemeʔ[r|ɾ]eaka[r|ɾ]akamu nana[r|ɾ]a nanake ʔusu
S.TRANSL: The people at home asked them in a hurry, "Did you see the orphan 'Usu?"

S.TRANSL: When we hold the ritual ceremony mikauŋu every year, we can't go without singing this song.

S.FORM: sua nikianara kaisisi mikaungu ia, niparanai tapucarakai nimuvua raape vina'e, tuutu emeka mata nanara 'usu.

S.TRANSL: The origin of the ritual ceremony came from the little people who gave (us) millet and bean seeds, and the orphan 'Usu.
